title: fix(idd): tryFetchBase hardcodes github.com, breaking GHES checkouts
body:
## Background

`tryFetchBase` in `src/scripts/branch-conflict-state.mts` (introduced in
commit 56dce2eb, predating #1398) hardcodes the fetch remote as:

```ts
const remote = `https://github.com/${owner}/${repo}.git`;
```

Found via Copilot/Codex review on PR #1452 (implementing #1398): for a
GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) repository, this always fetches from
github.com instead of the actual configured host, so the fetch fails
(or worse, could silently address an unrelated public github.com repo
of the same owner/repo name). This affects every caller of the shared
merge-base fallback-fetch path: the pre-existing conflict-probing used
for `CONFLICTING` / `BEHIND` states, and the new
`baseAdvancedSinceMergeBase` computation added in #1398 -- in both
cases, a GHES checkout with insufficient local history silently falls
back to an indeterminate/safe-default result instead of a working
fetch.

## Proposed change

Derive the remote from the configured `gh` host (e.g. `gh api` already
resolves against `GH_HOST` / `gh config get -h`) or from the local
checkout's `origin` remote URL, instead of hardcoding `github.com`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tryFetchBase` derives the remote host from configured `gh`
      host / local origin remote, not a hardcoded `github.com`.
- [ ] Existing github.com-hosted behavior unchanged (regression test).
- [ ] New test covering a non-github.com host resolves correctly (or
      documents why it cannot be tested without a live GHES instance).

Refs #1398
